budgets.replay_deadline_scope: context construction, query parse, solving, and binding/library identity checks; remaining milliseconds passed to Z3; late result cannot qualify

costs.accounting: Original campaign and entry phase timings are enclosed by the outer command cost; do not add them as additional costs. Audit time is separate. Static review and earlier tool reads are not measured by this field.

build_receipt.external_abi: scalar-only C functions; resource and multiple-result functions are internal
runtime_assumptions: Linux LP64 target with 64-bit pointers and size_t
C calloc returns null or an initialized nonaliasing allocation of the requested size
C malloc returns null or a fresh nonaliasing allocation of the requested size; bytes are initialized before read or remain unobserved
C free accepts a live allocation from calloc or malloc, or null
abort terminates execution; no cleanup after traps is promised
native compiler, linker, loader, libc and host hardware are trusted

limitations: This is an independent read-only consistency and scope audit, not a new SMT run, theorem proof, Lean check, compilation, candidate execution, or native measurement.

Totality means normal return for the selected exact public scalar call closure under its model. Five succeeded; div_floor remains unknown because its original closure has 34 blocks against the fixed 32-block cap.

All six lowering results concern the exact original pre-optimization LLVM internal bodies and original Core call closures. They do not prove optimized machine code, the C ABI wrapper, the C-to-Core translation, model/checker refinement, or whole-language soundness.
The full program and artifact retain 18 public exports. Twelve non-service exports were not selected for totality, and the six service error-return contract is not a theorem for all 18 exports.

Totality reports retain query hashes but the existing API does not retain their SMT text. Only the six lowering queries are available for byte-hash audit and the recorded fresh-solver replays; no totality-query replay is claimed.
Fresh-solver replay uses the same pinned Z3 implementation and retained query. It is not a second independent encoding or an independent theorem-proving kernel.

Replay identity before/after equality is recorded as a boolean backed by the hash-bound driver and each full lowering identity. The current binding and library files were independently rehashed without loading them; historical process identity and wall-time authenticity are not independently attested.
Hash and inventory consistency plus a retry-free exclusive-output driver support the one recorded attempt account. They cannot establish the absence of all unrecorded host activity.
The fixed time budgets are qualification deadlines with fail-closed late-result handling, not hard OS process-kill limits. All retained successful phases were below the budgets.

The existing canonical checker, independent symbolic encoders/parser, pinned solver, compiler, linker, loader, libc, ABI, and hardware remain explicit trusted or externally obligated components according to the respective scope.

single_attempt_evidence.scope: Retained archive and inspected driver consistently describe one invocation and one attempt per selected entry. This audit does not attest all unobserved host process history.

solver_identity.replay_identity_evidence: Each retained replay records the equality boolean against both fresh identity snapshots and the corresponding full lowering solver identity. The hash-bound driver implements that comparison; raw before/after replay identity objects are not separately serialized.
